'''Ousmane Dieng''' (born 21 May 2003) is a French professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[New Zealand Breakers]] of the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL). Standing at {{height|cm=208}}, he plays as [[forward (basketball)|forward]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ousmane Dieng |url=https://www.nzbreakers.basketball/player/3684/1668072/ousmane-dieng |website=nzbreakers.basketball |access-date=27 December 2021 |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life and youth career==
Dieng grew up in [[Lot-et-Garonne]], where his father, Ababacar, played basketball.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ousmane Dieng va jouer pour une équipe néo-zélandaise |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Basket/Actualites/Ousmane-dieng-va-jouer-pour-une-equipe-neo-zelandaise/1258233 |website=[[L'Équipe]] |access-date=2 June 2021 |language=French |date=2 June 2021}}</ref> At the youth level, he played for Villeneuve Basket Club and [[JSA Bordeaux Basket|JSA Bordeaux]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Le Villeneuvois Ousmane Dieng en route pour la NBA |url=https://www.ladepeche.fr/2020/12/01/le-villeneuvois-ousmane-dieng-en-route-pour-la-nba-9230351.php |website=[[La Dépêche du Midi]] |access-date=2 June 2021 |language=French |date=1 December 2020}}</ref> Dieng attended [[INSEP]] in [[Paris]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Cibola |first1=Christophe |title="La NBA est un objectif" |url=https://www.petitbleu.fr/2020/12/17/la-nba-est-un-objectif-9262265.php |website=Le Petit Bleu d'Agen |access-date=2 June 2021 |language=French |date=17 December 2020}}</ref> He competed for its under-18 team at the [[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament|Next Generation Tournament]].

== Professional career ==
In the 2020–21 season, Dieng averaged 12.6 points, 5.8 rebounds and 2.9 assists per game for [[Centre Fédéral de Basket-ball|Centre Fédéral]] in the [[Nationale Masculine 1]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Projected 2022 Lottery Pick Ousmane Dieng Becomes NBL Next Star with Breakers |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/projected-2022-lottery-pick-ousmane-dieng-becomes-nbl-next-star-with-breakers |publisher=[[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] |access-date=2 June 2021 |date=1 June 2021}}</ref>

On 1 June 2021, Dieng announced that he would play for the [[New Zealand Breakers]] of the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL) in the [[2021–22 NBL season|2021–22 season]], alongside fellow Frenchman and [[2022 NBA draft]] hopeful [[Hugo Besson]]. He became the first European player to join the league's Next Stars program to develop [[NBA draft]] prospects. Dieng had also been recruited by major [[college basketball]] programs and the [[NBA G League Ignite]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Wojnarowski |first1=Adrian |title=French 2022 NBA draft prospect Ousmane Dieng to play for New Zealand Breakers in NBL |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31547592/french-2022-nba-draft-prospect-ousmane-dieng-play-new-zealand-breakers-nbl |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=2 June 2021 |date=1 June 2021}}</ref> Dieng left the Breakers on 17 April 2022 in order to prepare for the [[2022 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Dieng, Besson Turn Attention to NBA Draft |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/dieng-besson-turn-attention-to-nba-draft |website=nbl.com.au |access-date=17 April 2022 |date=17 April 2022}}</ref>

==National team career==
Dieng represented [[France national under-17 basketball team|France]] at the [[2019 FIBA U16 European Championship]] in Italy. He averaged 8.9 points, 3.6 assists and 2.7 rebounds per game, helping his team win the silver medal.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Daniels |first1=Evan |title=French star Ousmane Dieng gaining high major interest |url=https://247sports.com/Article/Ousmane-Dieng-Arizona-Cincinnati-Oregon-State-Washington-State-147883567/ |website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=2 June 2021 |date=5 June 2020}}</ref>
